Air Spaces: getting the measure of air is an interdisciplinary project at The University of Manchester, bringing together social, health and atmospheric sciences with heritage studies. Combining air quality measurements with qualitative and creative approaches, the project explores how different communities and disciplines understand, experience and measure air.

Through research in homes and outdoor environments across Greater Manchester, we examine connections between indoor and outdoor air and inequalities in exposure to poor air quality. The project aims to make air quality measurement accurate, accessible and relevant, while supporting communities to articulate their concerns and engage with research and policy.

Sophie Woodward leads Air Spaces: Getting the Measure of Air. Her research explores everyday life, materiality and creative research methods.

Sophie is Professor of Sociology at The University of Manchester and Principal Investigator of the UKRI-funded Air Spaces: Getting the Measure of Air project (2026–2028). Her interdisciplinary work brings together sociology, anthropology and material culture to explore everyday lives and different ways of knowing about air.

She is Co-Director of the Morgan Centre for Research into Everyday Lives and a Fellow of the Academy of Social Sciences. She previously served as Vice-Director of the National Centre for Research Methods, leading its work on creative methods.
Everyday life; Materiality and material culture; Creative research methods; Air and atmospheres; Feminist theory
Hao Zhang uses AI and data-driven methods to understand present-day air quality variation and explore future scenarios.

Hao holds a PhD from The University of Manchester, where he trained through the EPSRC Centre for Doctoral Training in Aerosol Science. He also holds a master’s degree in Energy and Environmental Engineering from Zhejiang University.

His research applies advanced AI and data-driven methodologies to understand the complexities of air quality variation, both in the present and under future scenarios.
Air quality; Artificial intelligence; Data-driven methods; Future scenarios
Co-Investigator (Co-I) · Senior Lecturer in Atmospheric Sciences
Thomas Bannan studies indoor and outdoor air quality, using atmospheric measurements and sensor technologies to understand pollution and personal exposure.

Thomas is Senior Lecturer in Atmospheric Sciences at The University of Manchester and a Co-Investigator on Air Spaces: Getting the Measure of Air. His work examines atmospheric composition and chemistry, and their implications for health and climate.

He develops and applies chemical ionisation mass spectrometry to investigate trace gases and aerosols. His research also combines measurements in homes, sensor networks and data analysis to understand indoor pollution, personal exposure and inequalities, and to inform healthier buildings and air quality policy.
Indoor and outdoor air quality; Atmospheric chemistry; Air quality measurements; Personal exposure; Sensor networks
